subject: Biology
title: Breathing and Exchange of Gases
summary: Breathing do kaam hai: hawa andar-bahar (ventilation) aur gases ka exchange. Inspiration active hai — diaphragm aur external intercostal muscles contract hote hain, thorax ka volume badhta hai, pressure ghatta hai, hawa andar aati hai. Normal expiration passive hai.
Exchange sirf diffusion se hota hai, partial pressure ke gradient ke saath. CO₂ ka gradient chhota hai par wo O₂ se 20–25 guna zyada soluble hai, isliye aaram se diffuse hoti hai.
Transport: O₂ ~97% haemoglobin par (oxyhaemoglobin), ~3% plasma mein. CO₂ ~20–25% carbamino-haemoglobin, ~70% bicarbonate (carbonic anhydrase ki madad se), ~7% dissolved.
Control: medulla ka respiratory rhythm centre rhythm banata hai, pons ka pneumotaxic centre use moderate karta hai; chemosensitive area CO₂ aur H⁺ badhne par rate badhata hai.

formulas.name: Inspiratory capacity
formulas.when: Normal expiration ke baad kitni hawa andar le sakte ho.

formulas.name: Expiratory capacity
formulas.when: Normal inspiration ke baad kitni bahar nikal sakte ho.

formulas.name: Functional residual capacity
formulas.when: Normal expiration ke baad lungs mein bachi hawa.

formulas.name: Vital capacity
formulas.when: Forced inspiration ke baad maximum kitni bahar.
formulas.mistake: RV kabhi VC mein nahi aata.

formulas.name: Total lung capacity
formulas.when: Forced inspiration ke baad lungs mein total hawa.

formulas.name: Pulmonary ventilation
formulas.formula: Minute volume ≈ TV × breathing rate ≈ 500 mL × 12–16 = 6000–8000 mL/min

formulas.name: Gas delivery (NCERT)
formulas.formula: 100 mL oxygenated blood ⇒ ~5 mL O₂ tissues ko;  100 mL deoxygenated blood ⇒ ~4 mL CO₂ alveoli ko

examples.title: Volumes se capacities
examples.problem: TV = 500, IRV = 3000, ERV = 1100, RV = 1200 (mL). VC, TLC, FRC, IC?

examples.title: O₂ alveoli mein judti, tissues mein chhootti kyun?
examples.problem: Same haemoglobin do jagah ulta kaam kaise karta hai?
examples.solution: Alveoli: pO₂ zyada, pCO₂ kam, H⁺ kam, temperature kam ⇒ oxyhaemoglobin banta hai. Tissues: pO₂ kam, pCO₂ zyada, H⁺ zyada, temperature zyada ⇒ O₂ chhoot jaati hai (curve right shift).

examples.title: CO₂ chhote gradient par bhi tez kyun?
examples.problem: pCO₂ gradient sirf 45 → 40 mm Hg hai, phir bhi CO₂ exchange tez kyun?
examples.solution: CO₂ ki solubility O₂ se 20–25 guna zyada hai, isliye per unit partial pressure difference zyada CO₂ diffuse hoti hai.

topics.title: Mechanism of breathing
topics.explain: Inspiration: diaphragm + external intercostals contract ⇒ volume ↑ ⇒ intra-pulmonary pressure ↓ ⇒ hawa andar. Expiration: muscles relax ⇒ volume ↓ ⇒ hawa bahar. Zor se saans ke liye abdominal muscles bhi madad karte hain.

topics.title: Diffusion membrane
topics.explain: Alveolar wall, capillary wall aur unke beech basement substance — kul motai 1 mm se bhi bahut kam, isliye diffusion tez.

topics.title: Oxygen dissociation curve
topics.explain: Haemoglobin saturation vs pO₂ ka graph sigmoid (S-shaped) hota hai. pCO₂, H⁺ aur temperature badhne par curve right shift — O₂ aasani se chhoot-ti hai.

topics.title: CO₂ transport
topics.explain: RBC mein carbonic anhydrase: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ HCO₃⁻ + H⁺. Tissues mein ye aage ki taraf, alveoli mein peeche ki taraf chalta hai.

topics.title: Disorders
topics.explain: Asthma: bronchi/bronchioles mein inflammation, saans mein seeti. Emphysema: alveolar walls damage, surface area kam — main cause smoking. Occupational disorders: dust/silica se lungs ka fibrosis.

ratta: pO₂ / pCO₂ (mm Hg): atmosphere 159 / 0.3 · alveoli 104 / 40 · deoxygenated blood 40 / 45 · oxygenated blood 95 / 40 · tissues 40 / 45.
